transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-14
Start time: 09:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Morgan Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood), Ethan Kim (Redwood), Markus Havel (CinderPath CTO), Samira Ortiz (Head of Cloud Ops), Daniel Park (Security Architect), Leah Moore (PM), Ravi Patel (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick technical sync focused on: marketplace connector packaging, VPN peering and egress constraints, SLA expectations and metrics, KMS/HSM integration notes, and an initial plan for a pilot performance baseline. Customer has stricter egress rules and a corporate VPN hub; wants clear runbook for installation and SOC2-compatible audit logging.

Topics covered:
- Marketplace listing requirements and packaging (helm vs operator, container images, sidecar model)
- Private connectivity: VPN vs VPC peering vs dedicated interconnect
- SLA and telemetry collection points for 99.9% uptime target
- KMS integration patterns and key rotation policies
- Quantization/latency tradeoffs for pilot workloads
- Next steps for pilot and doc handoffs

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll do a quick agenda check — packaging, vpn/topology, sla metrics, kms, and pilot next steps. Is that all ok?
[00:18] Markus (CinderPath): Yeah that sounds good, uh, big thing for us is the vpn and firewall, we can't open broad egress.
[00:27] Samira (CinderPath): And we need to understand the marketplace listing side too — what our customers will see, and admin experience.
[00:35] Morgan (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll take the vpn/topology part. Priya will cover KMS and logging. Alex will talk marketplace packaging and pricing lanes.
[00:44] Leah (CinderPath): Quick ask — we have a SOC2 deadline in Q3 so any audit logging needs to be clear.
[00:52] Priya (Redwood): Noted. We'll show the audit events we emit and how to ship them to the customer's SIEM.

[02:05] Morgan (Redwood SE): So first, deployment patterns — we support two common patterns for marketplace customers: 1) a containerized connector bundled as a helm chart that runs in the customer's cluster, connects over an mTLS tunnel to Redwood control plane; 2) a sidecar/agent that talks to a private gateway in your VPC. There are tradeoffs.
[02:28] Daniel (CinderPath): The sidecar model sounds nice but our security team hates running extra privileged pods, so helm + limited egress is preferable.
[02:40] Morgan: Right — helm is the path most customers take. For limited egress we recommend an outbound-only proxy through a corporate NAT or through a trusted egress gateway.

[04:12] Ravi (CinderPath): For egress, we have an enterprise hub VPN — we prefer forced-tunnel to our SOC stack. Will that break anything with the redwood connector?
[04:22] Morgan: It shouldn't. We can support forced-tunnel as long as the traffic to Redwood's control plane endpoints is allowed. We also support static IPs for dedicated connector egress if you need a firewall rule. There was a note: sometimes customers see DNS weirdness if local resolver is overridden.
[04:42] Markus: DNS weirdness — can you expand? our ops team changed resolvers last month.
[04:48] Morgan: Sure — if your cluster resolves services differently or uses a DNS64 translate path it can cause TLS certificate validation issues for our control plane hostnames. We have two mitigations: 1) pin by IP (static egress IP) or 2) ship a small hosts override in the helm values. Both are a bit meh but workable.

[06:15] Alex (Redwood): On the marketplace side, packaging is mostly helm chart + OCI image. We can list in the public marketplace but also offer a private listing for enterprise customers. There's a separate listing checklist: security docs, SSO steps, install walkthrough, and a quickstart that we usually put as a runbook.
[06:34] Leah: For our customers we need to surface SSO (SAML) and per-tenant RBAC. Do you expose RBAC hooks?
[06:43] Ethan (Redwood): We do - our connector forwards identity assertions to the control plane and we support mapping to roles. For private deployment we recommend mapping to your IdP via SAML or OIDC; for hosted we support SSO into the Redwood Console.

[08:02] Samira: On SLAs, we are aiming at 99.9% for our own product that integrates your inference. What does Redwood guarantee on dedicated vs hosted?
[08:12] Alex: Hosted has a best-effort SLA today; dedicated reserved capacity can be SLA-backed at the contract level. For marketplace deployments we usually provide a recommended monitoring set and fallback logic if latency spikes. We can include SLOs in the docs but contractual SLA for marketplace listings needs a dedicated capacity commit.
[08:36] Markus: So to hit our 99.9 we might need reserved. We'll need numbers: p95 latency, token throughput per node, and what fallbacks look like.
[08:46] Morgan: We can share our performance profile spreadsheet — typical p95 for an MPT-style 8k seq at 90 tokens/sec on a 4-GPU rack is around X ms — (note: this transcript will include approximate numbers) — but for your workload we should run a baseline.

[10:05] Leah: Baseline run — what do you need from us?
[10:09] Priya: We'll need a small prompt set, sample payload sizes, and expected concurrency. Also your preferred quantization/model variant (we can recommend quantized variants to reduce memory).
[10:21] Daniel: Our typical calls are short single-turn prompts, 64–128 tokens, but we do batch scoring of candidate results. We expect bursts of ~200 concurrent requests during peak.
[10:32] Morgan: Ok, that helps. For bursts we'll talk about autoscaling and queue depth. For marketplace connector you may want a local cache for prefix results.

[12:00] Samira: About KMS — our security requires keys be customer-managed and rotated quarterly. How does Redwood integrate?
[12:10] Priya: We support external KMS with envelope encryption. For private deployment we can wire to your KMS/HSM via IAM roles and key policies; for hosted we provide a customer-managed key option where the key is in the customer's cloud KMS and Redwood only receives wrapped keys. Key rotation workflows are supported, but there is a standard window for rotation where old session tokens remain valid for N hours to ensure KV cache continuity.
[12:35] Daniel: That window could be a compliance problem. Can we shorten it?
[12:40] Priya: In many cases yes; we can propose a shorter rotation replay window at the cost of a small reconnection spike. We'll document mitigations.

[14:05] Markus: Does the marketplace listing need SOC2 artifacts?
[14:10] Alex: Yes, the listing checklist includes SOC2 type 2 attestation or a SOC2 report link, encryption details, RBAC/SSO steps, and operational runbooks. We also ask for a support contact and a contact for escalations.

[15:20] Leah: What's the recommended logging path? We use Splunk and want to ingest operation logs and audit events.
[15:28] Priya: We can stream audit events to your syslog/Splunk via a Kinesis/forwarder or push to your HTTP ingest endpoint. For connectors we emit events like install, config change, key use, and model rollout — timestamps and a correlation id so you can map across traces.

[17:00] Morgan: On the packaging side one choice is to run a sidecar for local caching and KV store — that improves cold-starts. But it may require persistent volumes which some orgs avoid. We often implement an optional sidecar for caching only.
[17:22] Ravi: Persistent volumes are avoided in our cluster for security reasons. Could we use ephemeral cache with a warmup job?
[17:30] Morgan: Yes, a warmup job on deploy is a common pattern — we can package that in the helm post-install hook.

[19:00] Alex: A note on pricing bands — marketplace listings usually have a connector fee plus usage. For enterprises we recommend a reserved capacity commit if they want guaranteed latency. I'll share examples in the follow-up.
[19:14] Markus: Good — our procurement will want a clear POC commercial option.

[21:05] Markus: On the private control plane: is there a pattern to run the control plane in our VPC or do you require Redwood control plane hosted?
[21:15] Ethan: We offer private control plane deployment for enterprise customers. It can be a managed appliance in your VPC (we run the control plane but it's isolated) or fully self-hosted on-prem for air-gapped environments. For marketplace listing often customers use the managed-private option.
[21:34] Samira: For the managed-private option, what's the upgrade process?
[21:38] Morgan: We do rolling upgrades with zero downtime for the control plane in most cases. For model runtime upgrades we do an orchestrated canary then promote. We will keep a runbook for rollback.

[23:00] Daniel: A couple of security nitpicks — do you support signed container images and image provenance?
[23:08] Priya: We support image signing via sigstore and can block unsigned images in the helm values. We'll include the signing verification step in the marketplace checklist.

[24:25] Alex: Back to the pilot: proposed timeline — week 0: exchange topology and access; week 1: deploy connector into staging with limited policy; week 2: run 24h baseline and collect telemetry; week 3: iterate on config and document the runbook. Does that align?
[24:42] Leah: That's workable. Procurement may push timelines but for technical it's fine.

[26:05] Morgan: A few gotchas we've seen with forced tunnel VPNs: 1) MTU issues causing TLS fragmentation; 2) Stateful firewall timeouts dropping long-lived model streams; 3) DNS intercept. We'll send a checklist for each.
[26:22] Ravi: MTU has bitten us before. We'll check our hub config.

[28:00] Markus: For SLA metrics, what telemetry points do we need to measure p95?
[28:06] Ethan: You'll want request latency per-route, token-generation times, error rates, pod-level CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, and health checks. We can provide a Grafana dashboard template.
[28:20] Samira: Will you ingest logs into our observability or use your SaaS?
[28:24] Alex: Both — for private deployments we push metrics to your Prometheus/Grafana; for hosted we provide a dashboard but you can also ship raw metrics to your monitoring.

[30:10] Leah: Any special license constraints for models shipped via marketplace?
[30:18] Morgan: Models come with their own licenses; we list approved models in our catalog. For enterprise you can pin model versions and we provide metadata for license compliance.

[31:40] Daniel: About quantization — we may accept minor degrade if it saves cost. What are the tradeoffs?
[31:48] Priya: Quantization reduces memory and can lower latency on certain hardware, but output fidelity can drift for some tasks. For scoring and short completion tasks it's often fine. We'll propose a quantization plan for your prompt set during the pilot.

[33:00] Markus: Any known issues with marketplace listing and cloud marketplace billing integration (e.g., Azure, GCP)?
[33:07] Alex: There are differences. Azure and AWS have different metering semantics — we map usage to tokens and connector-hours; we have lightweight billing adapters for marketplaces but the integration requires an SC product id and some billing metadata. We'll share a checklist for each marketplace.

[35:05] Morgan: One operational recommendation: enable a local NATS or redis for transient message buffering to avoid backpressure during spikes. It's optional but reduces tail lat.
[35:22] Ravi: We run redis in-cluster already.

[36:10] Samira: Are there any PII/PD concerns we must flag for our compliance team?
[36:16] Priya: We recommend treating request contents as potentially sensitive. For private deployments data never leaves your VPC. For hosted we have redaction tools and an option to pin customers to a private tenancy. We also redact logs by default and can provide field-level redaction in the pipeline.

[38:00] Alex: Quick pause — any blockers that would prevent the pilot?
[38:05] Markus: Our security team wants a written KMS integration plan and audit event examples.
[38:11] Daniel: And the VPC peering diagram — we'll provide that.

[40:02] Alex: Great. We'll attach the KMS integration template and the example events. Morgan, can you prepare the VPN checklist?
[40:08] Morgan: Yep — I'll put together VPN checklist, MTU, firewall rules, and sample iptables allowances.

[41:20] Leah: Also would like a short install video or 5-step quickstart for our internal docs team.
[41:27] Ethan: We'll record a 5–7 minute walkthrough and attach to the marketplace quickstart.

[43:00] Alex: Anything on procurement? We can propose a 30-day POC with a trial reserved pool for testing.
[43:08] Markus: Procurement will like a clear POC SOW and an exit clause after 30 days.

[44:30] Morgan: I'll set up a follow-up meeting for the baseline test — 30 minutes to run through deployment and start load. Proposed week of Apr 27.

[45:20] Samira: One last technical question — if we need to run inference on-prem for latency sensitive calls, is a hybrid mode supported?
[45:27] Priya: Yes — hybrid is supported. You can run the runtime on-prem closest to data and use the control plane for model management, or fully self-host for air-gapped. Both patterns are in our refarch.

[47:05] Ravi: A quick note — we use strict egress rules, but can we do an allowlist for a small set of IPs?
[47:12] Morgan: Yes, we can provide static egress IPs for the connector plus an optional NAT mapping.

[49:00] Alex: Recap — we will: 1) Morgan shares VPN checklist + helm sample (due 4/20); 2) Alex shares marketplace checklist + pricing examples (due 4/19); 3) Customer sends VPC peering diagram & firewall rules (due 4/18); 4) Priya shares KMS integration template and audit event examples (due 4/22); 5) Schedule baseline run week of 4/27.
[49:30] Leah: That covers it, thanks everyone.
[49:36] Markus: Thanks, look forward to the docs.
[49:40] Alex: We'll follow up in email with the links.
[50:02] END
